units.note: Course-level objectives printed under "General Objectives of Economics 30".

items.text: By studying Economics 30, the student should develop:
an understanding of the nature of Economics.
some ability to use certain Economics process skills.
an understanding and appreciation of the nature of the Canadian economy.
an understanding and appreciation of the nature of the Saskatchewan economy and its interrelationship with the Canadian economy.
an understanding and appreciation of the nature of the inter-national economy and its interrelationship with the Saskatchewan and Canadian economies.
an understanding of the role of the individual as a participant in the Saskatchewan, Canadian and international economies.
To give students an overview of the basic economic concepts of scarcity, choice and the marketplace.
Scarcity; wants; choice; capital goods, consumer goods; market; Gross National Product; producers; consumers; free goods; economic goods; utility and opportunity cost.
To gain an understanding of production, the reasons for specialization in our economy, and the interdependence of people, institutions and regions.
items.section: B. Production, Specialization and Exchange (Unit Two)

items.text: Specialization; interdependence; exchange; factors of production (1and, labor, capital, entrepreneurship); payment for factors (rent, interest, wages, profit); surplus, staple (primary products); barter; private property; and public property.
items.section: B. Production, Specialization and Exchange (Unit Two)

items.text: To assist students to gain an understanding of the organization, the operation and the problems of business institutions. *Units identified in parentheses refer to those in Economics 20.
Types of business organization (sole proprietorship, partnership, co-operative, corporation).
To give the student an understanding of the process of collective bargaining and the role unions play in the economy.
To provide the student with an understanding of the role of the market in the determination of prices and quantities.
items.section: E. The Role of the Market (Unit Five)

items.text: Market; price; supply; demand; consumer price index; and profit.
items.section: E. The Role of the Market (Unit Five)

items.text: To provide students with an understanding and appreciation of the role of money and financial institutions in the Canadian economy.
Banks; inflation and deflation; credit; currency; financial institutions; money; money supply; capital; cash flow; cash reserve; deposits; and savings.
To give students an understanding of the nature of a well-thoughtout savings and investment plan.
Risk; short-term investments; long-term investments; stock exchange; liquidity and capital gain.
To assist students in acquiring an appreciation of the role and importance of international trade in the Canadian economy. To provide an understanding of the nature of barriers to trade.

Foreign trade; comparative advantage; natural advantage; absolute advantage; balance of payments; protectionism; foreign investment; imports and exports--visible and invisible; tarrifs; and foreign exchange.
To give students an understanding of the role of government in the economy.
items.section: I. Role of Government in the Canadian Economy (Unit Nine)

items.text: Government revenue; government expenditures; taxation; income redistribution; government regulation; business cycle; monetary policy; and fiscal policy.
items.section: I. Role of Government in the Canadian Economy (Unit Nine)

items.text: To give students an understanding and appreciation of our own and alternative economic systems.
Capitalism; communism; private (or free) enterprise; socialism; and mixed economy (or mixed enterprise).
